hints: A route may use the half-price coupon at most once.
Track two distances per city: coupon unused and coupon already used.
For an edge of cost c, either travel normally in the same state or use floor(c/2) to move from unused to used.
analogy: Run shortest paths in a graph where each city has two versions: before and after spending the coupon.
example: A flight costing 9 can be taken for 4 with the coupon because integer division rounds down.
algorithm: Run Dijkstra on states (city,used). Relax normal cost c within each layer; from unused also relax floor(c/2) into used. Answer the used-state distance to n.
correctness: Every legal journey has a unique transition where the coupon is used; the two-layer graph represents exactly those routes, and Dijkstra finds their minimum cost.
complexity: O((n+m) log n) time and O(n+m) space.
